responseBinding.questionText: Which report has Mireille booked?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: a certificate with measurements and photographs

bindings.audiblePhrase: The detailed certificate. The brief note is for landlords who only want a visible-condition record; your insurer asked for measurements and photographs as well.

responseBinding.questionText: What should Mireille do before the inspector arrives?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Please clear the hall cupboard so the roof hatch opens fully. Leave the heavy stove in place, remove loose ash only when cold, and keep pets away from the work area.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the clay store?

bindings.audiblePhrase: The clay store is in the enclosed north-west corner, beyond the wash-up sink and against both the north and west walls.

responseBinding.questionText: Where are the pottery wheels?

bindings.audiblePhrase: From the entrance, walk north along the clean walkway and turn left before the central worktables. The pottery wheels occupy the western side beside those tables.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the glaze bench?

bindings.audiblePhrase: The glaze bench is on the eastern wall, directly south of the first-aid point. The counter immediately beside reception is only for collecting finished work.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the kiln room?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Continue to the fire door in the north-east corner. The kiln room is on the far side of that door. A ventilated mixing alcove lies before the door.

responseBinding.questionText: Where are the drying racks?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Finally, the drying racks stand just north of the central worktables and west of the clean walkway. They are open shelves rather than an enclosed room.

responseBinding.questionText: Which rule applies to the clay reclaim area?

bindings.audiblePhrase: At clay reclaim, keep scraps damp. Dry sweeping can put fine dust into the air, so use the wet-cleaning tools stored by the sink and close the reclaim tub after use.

responseBinding.questionText: Which rule applies to the glaze bench?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: Do not bring food or drink.

bindings.audiblePhrase: At the glaze bench, food and drink are not allowed. A covered water bottle may stay in your locker, but it should not be placed on a surface used for glaze materials.

responseBinding.questionText: Which rule applies to the kiln room?

bindings.audiblePhrase: The kiln room is restricted to trained staff. Members may leave labelled work on the loading shelf, yet they must not enter to adjust a firing schedule or open a hot kiln.

responseBinding.questionText: Which rule applies to the pottery wheels?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: Use the floor pedal only while seated.

bindings.audiblePhrase: At the pottery wheels, operate the floor pedal only while seated securely. Switch the wheel off before changing a bat or reaching underneath to retrieve a tool.

responseBinding.questionText: Which rule applies to the drying racks?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: Add the owner’s name and date.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Every piece placed on the drying racks needs the owner’s name and the date. The date helps us move work fairly when shelf space is limited.

responseBinding.questionText: Why do the students decide to use simulation actors?

bindings.audiblePhrase: So the main reason for actors is consistency. Each participant can receive the same fictional case and the same initial information before the communication method changes.

responseBinding.questionText: What will be the main outcome measure?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: recall of warning signs and follow-up action

bindings.audiblePhrase: Let us score recall of the warning signs and the follow-up action. Those details matter in the fictional discharge plan and can be checked against a clear rubric.

responseBinding.questionText: How will participants be allocated to conditions?

bindings.audiblePhrase: It would also mix the teaching time with the method. We should randomise within each session, using sealed cards prepared before participants arrive.

responseBinding.questionText: Why will the consultations be audio-recorded?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Audio is sufficient and less intrusive. More importantly, a second assessor can code a sample of recordings, so we can estimate whether the rubric is applied consistently.

responseBinding.questionText: What main change will be made after the pilot?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: The fictional case will be shorter.

bindings.audiblePhrase: So the key pilot change is to shorten the case, rather than asking actors to speak faster. The communication method should remain the feature we are comparing.

responseBinding.questionText: Actor prompt: describe your ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: A better prompt is: tell me your home plan. That invites the actor to explain what they will do without copying the student’s exact wording.

responseBinding.questionText: The rubric will include a category for ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: The rubric should credit accurate content even when the actor pauses and corrects an initial mistake. We can add a self-correction category instead of scoring only the first response.

responseBinding.questionText: Delayed recall will be tested after ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Twenty minutes is manageable. Participants can complete the satisfaction form during the interval, but they must not see the discharge sheet again.

responseBinding.questionText: The coding-sheet category hidden from the assessor is labelled ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: On the coding sheet, the category hidden from the recall assessor is labelled communication method. This prevents expectations from influencing the judgement.

responseBinding.questionText: Participants will be ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Second-year students offer a useful middle point. They have practised discharge conversations, yet the technique is unlikely to be automatic.

responseBinding.questionText: The organism’s ______ may remain after soft tissue decays.

bindings.audiblePhrase: When an organism dies, its soft tissues decay, but the shell can remain in peat. Identification therefore relies on durable structures rather than the living cell itself.

responseBinding.questionText: Species distributions are related to ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Different species tolerate different moisture conditions. Some are common where the water table lies close to the surface; others occur more often in comparatively dry microhabitats.

responseBinding.questionText: Testate-amoeba samples were taken every ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: In the cited peat-core study, testate-amoeba samples were taken every five centimetres. This spacing belongs to that proxy workflow and should not be confused with the denser schedule used for other evidence.

responseBinding.questionText: The target minimum is ______ tests per sample.

bindings.audiblePhrase: In the cited peat-core method, analysts used a light microscope and aimed to count a minimum of 100 tests in each sample whenever possible.

responseBinding.questionText: A ______ calibration links assemblages with measured conditions.

bindings.audiblePhrase: That modern calibration links changes in community composition with observed water-table depth. Statistical relationships summarise the pattern across many modern samples, not just one convenient site.

responseBinding.questionText: The transfer function estimates past ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: A transfer function applies the modern relationship to fossil assemblages. Its output is an estimate of past water-table depth, often accompanied by an uncertainty range.

responseBinding.questionText: What is the principal use of the testate-amoeba assemblage?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Testate amoebae mainly inform us about conditions at or near the peat surface. They are therefore valuable indicators of local water-table position, but they do not describe every process around the bog.

responseBinding.questionText: What does the pollen record directly identify?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Pollen is a classical proxy that directly identifies vegetation shifts. It provides a different line of evidence from the testate-amoeba reconstruction, so agreement between them can strengthen an interpretation without making the two records interchangeable.

responseBinding.questionText: What feature is associated with the plant-macrofossil record?

bindings.audiblePhrase: So, for plant macrofossils, the relevant feature here is continuous one-centimetre sampling. Do not confuse that method with the five-centimetre schedule used for pollen, microscopic charcoal and testate amoebae in the same study.

responseBinding.questionText: What is the stated use of the lipid-biomarker evidence?

bindings.audiblePhrase: In that study, lipid biomarkers were used to assess peatland composition, decomposition and restoration success. The authors also warned that one core per site and only three sampled depths limited both spatial and vertical resolution.
